{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish at the very start: a big body, nose on the left, forked tail on the right. It is an animal whose outline alone is recognizable to a judge who doesn't know our plan. I laid the start domino and built stroke 1, the top line, which is the stroke every other part of the picture depends on. The finished run connected all 111 standing dominoes to the start, so the full fish should fall.

Execution
I worked quietly on one piece: the start and the top line, carried on to the crossing near the tail neck. I flagged that the pad still showed the old start position, which kept me from tracing against the wrong layout. Near the end I inspected the area closely to confirm the chain was intact. Once everything was connected, I kept my hands off the crossing so I wouldn't risk a bump in the final minutes.

Collaboration
I split the work clearly at the outset: I took the top line, the bottom line and the tail went to teammates. I kept communication short and specific, and I offered to fix any gap if someone spotted one. I stayed out of other people's working areas, which mattered with the table this crowded.

Leadership
I set the direction in the first seconds by choosing the animal and the layout and assigning roles, which let the table start building without a long debate. Later I held steady on the plan, kept the table focused on a hands-off finish, and stayed calm as the clock ran down. I'd put my share of the result at about 30%: the concept, the start and the top line, and the final verification.", "my_share_percent": 30}
